findings.message: Duplicate numbers are only caught when both folders are in the same push (`duplicateNumbers(p.records)`). There is a second case this misses. A branch whose own folder reuses a number that `main` already synced under a different folder. The branch tree was cut before main gained that folder, so the branch push holds only one folder with that number. The push then overwrites the stored proposal, because the key matches and the commit is newer. Since 089, CI pushes every `specclaw/*` branch after each merge, so this now happens on its own. The PR number check would fail the PR, but CI syncs the branch before that PR merges. Fix: when the stored row's `source_ref` (the folder name written at line 107) is not `r.dir`, treat the record as a duplicate. Skip it with the same "two changes numbered NNN" line and set needsReview. Do the same in the self-sync.
findings.scenario: main has `089-quiet-hours`, synced as FLT-089 with source_ref `089-quiet-hours`. Branch `specclaw/089-agent-draft` was cut earlier and has a newer commit. CI pushes main, then the branch: `own` = `089-agent-draft`, key = FLT-089, no duplicate in its records, so FLT-089's title and phase become `089-agent-draft`'s. The next main push is skipped as stale (on the default branch, so it reads Needs you), and the main change stays hidden behind the branch's.

findings.message: Self-sync withdrawal now depends on `refOf()` removing `@<sha>` from each record's source. It only removes 7–40 hex characters. `--sha` is never checked, so a shorter or non-hex commit leaves the sha inside the ref. The stored source never matches the next run's ref, and every gone folder is quietly left in place with no 'held' line. Before this diff, withdrawal did not depend on the ref. The test fix that changed `main@3` to `main@33333333` shows the problem. Fix: refuse a `--sha` that isn't `/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i`, as PushInput does, or resolve it with `git rev-parse`.
findings.scenario: Run `sync:specclaw --sha abc123`, delete folder 103 on main, then run `sync:specclaw --sha def456`. refs = {`main@def456`} and the stored source is `main@abc123`, so FLT-103 is never eligible. The result is withdrawn 0 with nothing skipped, and the proposal stays live.

findings.message: Confirming a held mass withdrawal checks only the count, not which proposals would be withdrawn. Between the hold and the confirming run (a manual CI dispatch), a different set of proposals of the same size can be withdrawn without anyone seeing it. Fix: confirm with a value that depends on the held key set, such as a short hash of the sorted keys, and show it in the hold message.
findings.scenario: The hold names 5 proposals (FLT-102…106). Before the person dispatches `confirm_withdraw=5`, a merge restores 104 and deletes 108. The confirm then withdraws a different 5 (102, 103, 105, 106, 108), and 108 was never shown to anyone.

findings.message: The server takes `withdrawMissing: true` on trust. Anyone with `delivery:proposal:push` can send a partial record set from the default branch and withdraw up to half of the eligible proposals (more than 2) without a hold. The tool description says the flag is only for a push that carries every change, but nothing enforces it. Withdrawal is a reversible meta flag, so this is minor. Consider holding any withdrawal from a non-CI caller, or requiring confirmWithdraw whenever keys > 0.
findings.scenario: A plugin user on main sends records for 6 of 10 proposals with withdrawMissing: true. 4 proposals are withdrawn with no hold, because 4 ≤ max(2, 5).

findings.message: When CI splits a push of more than 200 changes into batches and a duplicate pair falls across the boundary, the server only sees the client's `duplicate` flag. The skip line then names one folder ("two changes numbered 074: 074-a"). Either keep a number's folders in the same batch in specclaw-sync-ci.mjs, or word the message so it doesn't depend on seeing both folders.
findings.scenario: There are 201 changes and the pair 200-a/200-b straddles the batch boundary. Each batch reports "two changes numbered 200: 200-a" (or 200-b) on its own.
